report:
Finding: Model B appears to be domain-shifted toward culinary/food/restaurant/blog content relative to Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (layers ~18–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by “restaurant/Restaurant,” “cooking/Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking,” “Cake,” “kitchen,” “Cafe,” “Food,” and “blog/blogs/blogger/Blog,” along with list/heading-like tokens (“Professional,” “International,” “No,” “www,” “:”, numbers). Earlier large-norm cells also show related tokens like “Cook,” “Chef,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “restaurant(s).”
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in later layers (especially from L18 onward, peaking at L25) where those culinary/blog tokens recur across positions, indicating a strong late-layer bias in B toward that domain.

Conclusion: Model B is likely fine-tuned or otherwise biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant/blog-style web text; Model A lacks this bias.
